title: Connect the complete approved navigation and match journey in the actual App
prompt: Read README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/PILOT100_BACKLOG.md and the exact referenced imported design sections before editing. RULES-SPEC-v1.md is canonical for production mechanics: six-node Repair/Sabotage tracks, one-person crew votes, Route/Gate operations, deterministic powers and silent spectators. SCREEN-FLOW prototype 5/5 scores and hardcoded transitions are UX references only. Preserve historical T01–T10 APIs/tests; implement the new view version in new game-v1 modules instead of silently changing legacy five-mark boards or command parsers. Use black/charcoal/neutral-frost chrome and full-colour approved expressive content through semantic asset keys. Modal-first means the complete game background is uniformly blur/dim/desaturated and inert; the fixed platform banner dock remains mounted outside that game viewport. No visible accounts/login, telemetry, credentials, live Firebase, ad SDK or unreviewed asset downloads. Keep local presentation distinct from authority: clients display server/solo-engine phases and deadlines, never compute secret outcomes, choose timeout targets, advance multiplayer on a local clock or reveal another alignment. Use injected semantic media/ad/purchase ports; no direct SDK playback or billing calls from UI. Edit only ownership, use original fixtures, run scoped tests/lint/typecheck and npm run check. DOM tests use jsdom, explicit afterEach(cleanup), Vitest and current Testing Library. Report results and contract changes; do not commit, push, open PRs, deploy or spend on providers. Wire the approved production screens into the actual application, preserving legacy module tests. Launch/alias-avatar leads to Home, Play selects Solo setup or multiplayer directory, create/join reaches lobby, acknowledged start runs entry/reveal/City Board, and authoritative phases open vote/operation/resolution/City Moment/targets/Match End. Keep modal-first background lock, one clear action and stable dock at the root. Local Solo uses the reviewed engine/bot adapter with no Firebase dependency; multiplayer uses the versioned authenticated session port. Compose support navigation/settings/achievements/help and safe leave/reconnect flows. Production never imports hardcoded prototype outcomes/timers. Add explicit client dependency/SDK bootstrap coordination before editing manifests owned elsewhere. Offline Solo must be fully reachable without a Firebase project, native ads/purchases or approved final artwork. An unavailable live multiplayer capability shows the real gate and must not fabricate connected cloud participants. Optional achievement progress/native purchases use safe unavailable/no-op states. Explicitly labeled preproduction visual placeholders are allowed for local flow review; production shipping art/provenance remains gated in A100. The owner has supplied this design pack as the approved screen/rules direction; no additional generic wireframe approval is required to implement its documented flows. External art approval applies only to final asset delivery.
acceptance: Every listed route, overlay and return path is reachable in the real App with no visible login and correct mode distinction.
One complete local Solo fixture uses real deterministic engine/bot adapters; multiplayer fixtures follow authoritative phase/recipient updates without browser outcomes.
Role/Ghost/operation secrets, direct card-vote semantics, power targets and silent spectators remain correct across navigation and snapshot changes.
App-wide modal lock, banner persistence, semantic media, accessibility focus and failed/canceled navigation behave together in DOM flow tests.
Missing Firebase, native ad/IAP adapters, unapproved final art or optional achievement rules cannot block the complete offline Solo route; unavailable capabilities are explicit and never faked.
Preproduction placeholders are visibly labeled and replaceable by semantic keys; the handoff distinguishes flow acceptance from final visual approval/shipping readiness.
designSections: SCREEN-FLOW: Ruta de primer uso, all numbered and support surfaces; SWARM-BRIEF: G2 Local vertical slice
